categories.definition: Gives the agent a pre-built mental model of what the project is, where things live, and how its parts behave, so it can locate and understand code without exploratory reading.
includes: project overview / purpose statements
directory trees, module maps, 'where to look' tables, key-files tables
architecture descriptions (layers, processes, data flow, package dependency graphs)
tech-stack and dependency inventories, platform support matrices
API/semantics mini-reference: component prop tables, plugin protocol method tables, fixed-point format tables, config file locations, env-var tables
project terminology definitions used descriptively
excludes: runnable command blocks belong to command-recipes — the agent executes those, it only reads a map
symptom-keyed caveats ('X fails because Y, do Z') belong to trap-notes even when they describe the environment
pointers that say 'read file X for area Y' belong to context-dispatch — the map contains content, a pointer routes to it
discriminators: Does the agent consume this text by reading it to orient (map), or by executing it (recipe)?
Is the description neutral ('what is'), or keyed to a known mistake with a corrective ('watch out, do this instead')? Neutral → map, corrective → trap-notes.

examples.quote: SQLite rewrite in Rust. 40+ crate workspace.
Multi‑window Electron app. Every window runs the *same* JS bundle but plays a different role
**`BLButton`** — Base `UIControl` with blur background and focus-driven parallax + shadow. Use `onPrimaryAction` callback instead of `addTarget`.

categories.definition: Hands the agent copy-paste executable invocations and step sequences (build, test, lint, run, release, environment setup) so it never has to rediscover how to operate the project.
includes: fenced command blocks with flags and inline comments
command → purpose tables
numbered operational procedures (patch export flow, release flow, tag maintenance, PR-conflict recovery)
environment/tooling setup steps (uv venv, poetry, bundle install, corepack enable)
excludes: commands mandated as a precondition for claiming done or committing belong to completion-gates — same text, different job
prescriptions about how to sequence one's own work (TDD, plan-first, branch flow) belong to work-process
discriminators: Is the command offered as how-to for when the agent needs it (recipe), or mandated as a gate before done/commit (completion-gate)?
Does the block give literal steps of domain work (recipe), or select which resource/tool/context to engage (context-dispatch)?

examples.quote: make run                          # Backend with hot reload (localhost:3000, admin/admin)

# Always use `uv` for Python environment management:
uv venv --python 3.12
source .venv/bin/activate
gh run download <run-id> --repo electron/electron --name update-patches

categories.definition: Normalizes the surface form of everything the agent produces — code, commits, prose — so its output reads as native to the project.
includes: naming conventions (files, variables, tests, branches)
import ordering, comment/docstring policy, formatting and line-length rules
commit-message and PR-title formats (conventional commits, scopes, sign-off syntax as format)
controlled vocabulary ('use these terms verbatim', spelling of names)
language/idiom preferences (never-nesting, functional-first, error-handling idioms)
excludes: rules whose violation breaks behavior, data, or policy belong to hard-constraints — style violations merely look non-native
value-laden tradeoff guidance ('simplicity first') belongs to engineering-values — style rules are mechanically checkable
discriminators: If violated, does something break or a policy get breached (hard-constraint), or does the diff merely look foreign (style)?
Can conformance be checked mechanically from the artifact alone (style), or does it require judgment about tradeoffs (values)?

examples.quote: **Single-word file names** whenever possible (e.g., `permissions.ts`, `capabilities.ts`, `service.ts`).
IMPORTANT: all comments except godoc comments must be lowercase, test messages must be lowercase, log messages must be lowercase
**Naming Convention**: Use `camelCase` for variable names in JavaScript/TypeScript. Avoid `snake_case`

categories.definition: Removes options from the agent's action space outright: targets it must never touch, tools it must never use, invariants it must never break — no human can unlock them mid-task.
includes: forbidden tools/commands ('never use npx', 'never npm — always pnpm', 'never --release')
forbidden targets (generated output, snapshots, versioned docs, i18n files, upstream golden tests)
artifact invariants (deps pinned exactly, every table has companyId, writes only through the lock module)
secret/credential prohibitions ('never commit secrets', 'no tokens in logs or snapshots')
excludes: actions permitted after asking belong to human-loop-contract ('ask before X' vs 'never X')
prohibitions whose content prescribes the legitimate work sequence ('never commit to main — use a PR') belong to work-process
cosmetic requirements belong to house-style
discriminators: Is the action forbidden unconditionally (constraint), or allowed once a human approves (human-loop-contract)?
Does the rule fence off a target/tool (constraint), or route the agent onto an approved workflow path (work-process)?

examples.quote: **Never use `npx`.** It is considered dangerous because it can silently fetch and execute arbitrary packages from the registry.
**E2E snapshots** (`waspc/e2e-tests/test-outputs/snapshots/`) must never be manually edited.
Never expose cross-tenant data or skip `companyId` scoping.

categories.definition: Shapes the sequence and method of the agent's work — how to start, slice, branch, iterate, and log — rather than the content of the artifact itself.
includes: TDD cycles ('write a failing test first'), plan-first / plan-mode entry rules
small-diff / vertical-slice / one-phase-at-a-time discipline
branch-and-PR flow, trunk-based rules, branch naming tied to flow
mandated work logging (append to CHANGELOG-AI.md, update lessons.md, keep Status.md current)
excludes: terminal checks before claiming done belong to completion-gates — process shapes the path, gates check the end state
companion edits to other artifacts belong to coupled-change-obligations
community-acceptability rules for the contribution itself (duplicate checks, AI disclosure) belong to ai-contribution-governance
discriminators: Does the block prescribe a concrete sequence/procedure for doing the work (process), or a tradeoff criterion requiring judgment (engineering-values)?
Is the obligation about how work proceeds (process) or about what must pass at the end (completion-gates)?

examples.quote: 1. Write a failing test that demonstrates the desired behavior or reproduces the bug
Work in **very small vertical slices** - the smallest shippable increment
**Never commit directly to `main`.** All changes must go through a feature branch and pull request

categories.definition: Pre-loads hard-won empirical knowledge — known failure modes, misleading defaults, environment quirks — each keyed to a symptom or mistake with its corrective, so the agent doesn't lose time in a known trap.
includes: symptom → cause → fix triplets ('jsxDEV is not a function → set web.output single')
misleading tool defaults ('yarn test includes --watch by default')
environment/PATH/hosting quirks (Cursor Cloud PATH injection, poetry not on PATH non-interactively, localhost vs 127.0.0.1)
'this is a common mistake' callouts (BASE_PATH only breaking after deploy)
version-compatibility pin tables born from past breakage
excludes: neutral environment description with no trap belongs to codebase-map
end-user troubleshooting for the product's own users (obfuscator option tuning) is residual or map, not an agent trap
discriminators: Is the note anticipatory/corrective, keyed to a concrete failure the agent would otherwise hit (trap), or a neutral description (map)?
Does it warn about a trap and give a workaround (trap-note), or forbid an action outright (hard-constraint)?

examples.quote: The `yarn test` script includes `--watch` by default. Always use `yarn jest --no-watch` or add `--watchAll=false` to run tests once and exit.
`_reactJsxDevRuntime.jsxDEV is not a function` ... **Fix**: In `app.json`, set `"web": { "output": "single" }`
use `http://localhost:5173`, not `http://127.0.0.1:5173` (the latter refuses the connection)

categories.definition: Routes the agent to the right resource at the right moment — which deeper doc to read, which skill to load, which tool/subagent/model to engage — without inlining the content itself.
includes: task → guide routing tables and directory-scoped AGENTS.md pointers
conditional reading triggers ('read tests/CLAUDE.md when touching coverage', 'do not load it for ordinary feature work')
skill catalogs with load/invoke conditions, @doc imports
tool-selection mandates ('use search-docs before other approaches', 'use context7 when working with bunqueue')
delegation/model-routing/subagent policy ('use subagents liberally', 'route code to executor with model=opus')
persona/mode activation blocks (trigger word → enter orchestrator mode)
excludes: the routed-to content itself, when inlined, belongs to its own category (map, recipes, etc.)
literal steps of domain work belong to command-recipes — dispatch selects the instrument, recipes wield it
discriminators: Does the block point elsewhere with a trigger condition (dispatch), or contain the substantive content (map/recipe)?
Does it name a resource to engage as an instrument — doc, skill, tool, subagent (dispatch) — or give the literal steps of the work (recipe)?

examples.quote: IMPORTANT: Before any research or coding, match the task to this table. A single task often maps to **multiple rows** — read **all** matching guides before starting.
Load relevant skills before starting; reload when scope changes mid-session.
You must use this tool to search for Laravel-ecosystem documentation before falling back to other approaches.

categories.definition: Defines what must pass before the agent may claim done or commit — the checks, checklists, and evidence that gate completion.
includes: 'always run X after every code change' mandates
'run the full build script before committing — dotnet test alone is not enough'
pre-PR quality checklists, RSN-must-pass gates
evidence requirements ('run the command, read the output, then state the result'; 'verify before claiming completion')
excludes: the same commands offered as optional how-to belong to command-recipes
obligations to co-edit sibling artifacts belong to coupled-change-obligations — gates run checks, sync rules make edits
discriminators: Is the command mandated as a precondition for done/commit (gate), or offered as reference for when needed (recipe)?
Does the obligation say 'run a check' (gate) or 'also update artifact Y' (coupled-change)?

examples.quote: Always run backend tests after every code change: `cd backend && poetry run pytest`.
**IMPORTANT:** Always run the full `build.ps1` script before committing changes. `dotnet test` alone may pass while the full build fails
Never claim work is complete without running verification commands. Evidence before assertions — run the command, read the output, then state the result.

categories.definition: Obligates companion edits whenever one artifact changes — 'when you change X, also update Y in the same change' — preserving cross-artifact consistency the repo cannot enforce automatically.
includes: docs-must-track-behavior rules (README/MkDocs/--help updated in the same PR)
N-piece rules (component + story + test; skill + README entry + plugin.json + docs page)
design-token ↔ token-doc sync tables, roadmap-slide ↔ deck-structure sync
multi-file registration drift rules (update install.sh + update-hyprland.sh + dry-run-build.sh together)
mandatory indirect channels for a coupled artifact (translations via Crowdin, manual port to cloudflare-docs)
excludes: run-a-check requirements belong to completion-gates
logging one's own work (changelog/lessons entries) belongs to work-process — sync rules mirror a content change into a sibling artifact
discriminators: Is the obligation triggered by a change to artifact X and discharged by editing artifact Y (sync), or by running a verification (gate)?
Does the companion artifact describe the same content (sync), or record the process of working (work-process logging)?

examples.quote: Whenever you add, remove, or change any of the following, update `DesignTokens.mdx` in the same change
whenever you add, rename, remove, or change how a user-reachable skill fits the flows, re-read `ask-matt`'s `SKILL.md` and update it so the map stays accurate
If you touch module ordering or add a new component, update `install.sh` (sequence + option), `update-hyprland.sh` (`DEFAULT_MODULES`), and `dry-run-build.sh` (`DEFAULT_MODULES`) to prevent drift.

categories.definition: Gives the agent decision criteria for open-ended tradeoffs — value orderings, quality philosophy, and the project's current posture — where no mechanical rule can decide.
includes: value orderings ('crash > corrupt', 'a failed command that preserves data beats a successful one that destroys work')
minimalism/simplicity/reuse-first doctrine ('minimum code, nothing speculative', '先用现成的')
epistemic norms ('validate your hypotheses', 'assert invariants, don't hedge')
project posture calibration ('maturing mode — balance clean design with compatibility', 'stable/maintenance — no major features', recommended-use-cases ✅/⚠️ lists)
excludes: mechanically checkable rules belong to house-style or hard-constraints
concrete procedures belong to work-process — values inform judgment, they don't sequence steps
discriminators: Does applying the block require weighing tradeoffs (values), or is compliance checkable from the artifact (style/constraint)?
Does it calibrate what kind of change is welcome (posture/values), or prescribe how to carry a change out (process)?

examples.quote: **Correctness paramount.** Production DB, not a toy. Crash > corrupt
Never risk data loss without explicit user consent. A failed command that preserves data beats a "successful" one that silently destroys work.
**Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**

categories.definition: Governs the live dialogue between agent and operating human: which actions need approval first, when to stop and ask, and in what form and tone to communicate.
includes: approval gates on actions ('before git push, stop and get explicit human approval'; 'ask before reducing scope / changing schema')
escalation-and-refusal rules ('if the guide conflicts with the request, refuse the change and explain why'; 'report the problem and ask for guidance')
question-form mandates (AskUserQuestion with 2-4 options, no prose question dumps)
communication style and address ('be concise in explanations', '每次和我沟通，叫我【帅哥】')
division of labor ('leave the user to run these commands', 'ask the user for the version number')
excludes: unconditional prohibitions belong to hard-constraints — here the action is allowed after asking
rules aimed at project maintainers/reviewers rather than the live operator belong to ai-contribution-governance
discriminators: Is the action's blocker a human's live consent (human-loop), or is it never allowed at all (hard-constraint)?
Does the rule govern dialogue with the operating user (human-loop), or acceptability of the artifact to the project community (governance)?

examples.quote: Before running `git push`, stop and get explicit human approval. ... "Open a PR" in a task description is intent, not permission to push without review.
需要你向我提问时，必须使用选项列表，禁止用散文/段落罗列问题。
Ask before reducing scope, changing architecture, changing public contracts, or adding production dependencies.

categories.definition: Makes the agent's contribution acceptable to the project's human community: accountability, disclosure, anti-slop hygiene, and PR metadata policy that exist because the contributor is (or uses) an AI.
includes: human-accountability mandates ('pure code-agent PRs are not allowed', 'you are responsible for quality and correctness')
duplicate-work checks and no-busywork/no-farming policies with fail-closed behavior
AI-noise cleanup requirements and AI-use disclosure in PR descriptions
PR metadata policy (semver/backport labels, mandatory Notes: sections, DCO sign-off, 'never mention Claude in commits')
evidence-for-reviewers requirements ('include dry-run logs when fixing installer issues')
excludes: how to sequence one's own work belongs to work-process
live-operator approval rules belong to human-loop-contract — governance addresses the asynchronous review community
discriminators: Is the rule about the contribution's acceptability to maintainers/community, especially as AI-assisted work (governance), or about the work's method (process)?
Would the rule exist if the contributor were a trusted human employee? Duplicate-PR checks, AI disclosure, anti-farming would not — governance.

examples.quote: Pure code-agent PRs are **not allowed**. A human submitter must understand and defend the change end-to-end.
❌ **Don't**: Use AI for contribution farming or trivial changes.
PR bodies must always include a `Notes:` section as the **last line** of the body. This is a consumer-facing release note

residual.description: Blocks with no discernible job for a coding agent: human-audience README copy pasted wholesale (license text, sponsorship/community/support sections, project statistics, marketing feature lists), changelog-of-this-file history tables, end-user product support content, and fragments too terse to carry intent. Concentrated in one file (javascript-obfuscator's 45KB doc-dump contributes roughly half of all residual blocks) plus scattered history tables (PVE-Tools 变更记录) and the 324-byte RPG-JS fragment's stray first line.
examples: javascript-obfuscator 'Support and Community: GitHub Sponsors: Direct sponsorship'
PVE-Tools-9 '变更记录 (Changelog)' table of past CLAUDE.md regenerations
RSamaium/RPG-JS 'View content of CONTRIBUTING.md' (bare pointer with no trigger or subject)

observations: Provenance is visibly trimodal — hand-authored, tool-generated, and vendor-injected — and it predicts content mix better than star count: nunomaduro/whyphp.dev is entirely Laravel Boost vendor boilerplate, TennyZhuang/iter-chunks reads as a generator's 'Repository Guidelines' template, onevcat/Kingfisher's AGENTS.md still carries the '# CLAUDE.md / This file provides guidance to Claude Code' header verbatim (a straight file copy), and digoal/blog concatenates a repo-specific file with a second generic '# CLAUDE.md' community rule-pack — people paste circulating rule-packs wholesale.

ai-contribution-governance appears almost exclusively in high-star infrastructure repos that receive unsolicited AI PRs (vllm 87k, electron 122k, juice-shop 13k, RSSHub 45k): duplicate-work checks, 'pure code-agent PRs are not allowed', anti-farming, fail-closed refusal. Low-star personal repos never carry it; their files instead optimize a single trusted operator's throughput (houbb even auto-approves all file changes and command executions — the exact opposite posture).

In agent-tooling repos the file stops being documentation and becomes the runtime program itself: oh-my-claudecode ships delegation policy, model routing, hook-pattern grammars and kill switches inside XML-ish tags; planckatron-claude-code is a persona bootloader (trigger word → splash screen → orchestrator mode). The same filename spans 'notes about the code' to 'the product's executable behavior'.

Several files instruct the agent to maintain the very knowledge base it reads — a self-updating loop: carbon's '.ai/lessons.md' (Context → Problem → Rule → Applies to), CarGuo's mandatory CHANGELOG-AI.md appends, worktrunk/clincus 'update the relevant rule when you learn something durable'. Trap-notes sections read as the sediment of this loop ('mismatches have caused repeated CI failures'), i.e. institutional memory accumulating in-file.

Coupled-change sync obligations cluster exactly where CI cannot see: cloudflare/agents states 'there is no automated sync workflow. Changes here must be manually ported'; where a checker exists the block instead documents the checker and its blind spot (formspec explains why plain api-extractor would trivially pass and CI diffs the regenerated reports instead). The category is a map of each repo's un-automated invariants.

Contradictory philosophies coexist across files with equal confidence, so an agent hopping repos must treat every rule as local: LibreChat mandates heavy mocking avoidance and 'never use any' TypeScript strictness while streamlabs declares strictNullChecks intentionally OFF repo-wide; postgres-ai bans any mention of Claude in commits while turso and vllm require AI co-author trailers; quii bans manual verification scripts in favor of tests while houbb bans mid-implementation verification runs entirely.
